identity.title: Tumor-area mitosis proportion as an image-derived mitotic phenotype in lung squamous cell carcinoma: Patient-level prognostic and multi-omics evaluation.

content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitotic activity is a recognized marker of tumor proliferation, yet its reproducible assessment across whole-slide images (WSIs) remains difficult. We developed a transfer-learning framework for lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) and evaluated whether a patch-derived tumor-area mitosis proportion (TAMP) was associated with survival and molecular tumor characteristics. METHODS: The analysis combined MIDOG 2022 with TCGA-LUSC, including 478 patients and 512 diagnostic WSIs after quality control. Tumor regions and mitotic figures were reviewed by two pathologists with interobserver agreement of Cohen's kappa >/= 0.85. A ResNet-50 model was trained on MIDOG and subsequently adapted to TCGA-LUSC using Focal Loss and stain-aware augmentation. Target-domain performance was evaluated using patient-level stratified 5-fold cross-validation and an additional WSI-level holdout analysis to address potential leakage from the initial patch-level partitioning. TAMP was calculated from patient-level out-of-fold predictions as the proportion of evaluable tumor patches classified as mitosis-positive. Associations with overall survival, immune and genomic features, transcriptomic programs, predicted drug response, and transcription-factor activity were subsequently examined. Multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, smoking status, tumor stage, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status. RESULTS: The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.975 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.965-0.980) on the held-out MIDOG test set. In TCGA-LUSC, fine-tuning increased the initial patch-level AUC from 0.82 to 0.92. Patient-level cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.89 (95% CI: 0.86-0.90), and WSI-level holdout validation yielded an AUC of 0.90 (95% CI: 0.84-0.90). High TAMP was associated with poorer overall survival (log-rank p = 0.008; HR = 1.82, 95% CI: 1.18-2.81) and remained associated with mortality after multivariable adjustment (adjusted HR = 1.68, 95% CI: 1.08-2.62; p = 0.022). Higher TAMP was also associated with lower stromal fraction, selected immune-cell differences, greater indel-derived neoantigen load and indel burden, and enrichment of stem-cell proliferation, growth-factor-response, E2F-target, G2M-checkpoint, and MYC-target programs. Additional associations were observed with predicted sensitivity to selected cell-cycle-targeting compounds and with proliferation-related transcription-factor activity. CONCLUSIONS: TAMP provides a patient-level, image-derived representation of mitosis-positive tumor regions that was associated with survival and several molecular features in TCGA-LUSC. Its association with overall survival persisted after adjustment for major clinical covariates. External multicenter validation, prespecified threshold evaluation, and prospective assessment are required before clinical use.
